QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_13

question.text: Grameen Swasthya NPO ran a rural cataract-surgery camp under SAS-200 across 200 villages; it screened 50,000 people and performed 5,000 surgeries (85% improved-vision outcome). The programme is co-funded by the State Blindness Control Programme (SBCP). The SIA Ms. Priya Shah is evaluating attribution. The MOST defensible approach is:

answer.text: Claim 100% of the 5,000 surgeries as the NPO's attributable impact since it is the direct implementer
Report 50% attribution as a conservative rule of thumb without evidence
Use only CSR-donor-facing narrative numbers and ignore SBCP overlap
Deduct deadweight (what would have happened anyway under SBCP) and displacement, and report NET additional impact of the NPO's programme

explanation.text: **The Logic:** SAS-200 assessment requires subtracting deadweight (outcomes that would have occurred even without the programme) and displacement (shifting surgeries from SBCP queues) to isolate NET additional impact. Simply claiming total output is common but methodologically wrong when a parallel government scheme exists. **The Trap:** Option A is the most frequent attribution error — it double-counts SBCP surgeries. Option C hides the overlap. Option B is a rule-of-thumb that the SIA must justify with data, not assume. **Cross-Exam Context:** Attribution-vs-contribution debate also appears in X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser — CSR advisory) and XII (Securities Markets Foundation — market vs stock returns attribution). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** For attribution under SAS-200, build a 2x2 table: (NPO-only villages vs SBCP-plus-NPO villages) x (pre vs post). The difference-in-differences gives you NET impact net of deadweight.
